Today, our X-59 quiet supersonic X-59 aircraft traveled from Birmingham, Alabama, to Daytona Beach, Florida. The aircraft aims to fly faster than sound with just a gentle thump rather than a sonic boom — helping usher in a new era of faster air travel.

tweets.text: @Space_Station @astro_anil @csa_asc NASA astronaut @Astro_Anil and @CSA_ASC astronaut are now safely in the airlock following their successful spacewalk. Astronauts @Astro_Watkins and Luke Delaney are waiting inside the @Space_Station to assist them out of their spacesuits. https://t.co/W8ujUN6xlf

tweets.author: @NASA
tweets.text: @Space_Station @astro_anil @csa_asc Now that the solar array has been successfully deployed, @Astro_Anil and Joshua Kutryk of @CSA_ASC will now clean up their work sites and head back to the airlock of the @Space_Station. https://t.co/LEWEzJ6RDm

tweets.author: @NASA
tweets.text:
@Space_Station @astro_anil @csa_asc The final solar array is installed — and now unfurling.
 
When this solar array is completely deployed, the @Space_Station will generate approximately 215 kW, boosting the orbiting laboratory’s power by up to 30%. https://t.co/YJ4eYTEEJ4

tweets.author: @NASA
tweets.text:
@Space_Station @astro_anil @csa_asc POV: Your office is in the sky. 
 
@Astro_Anil is seen moving toward his spacewalk teammate, Joshua Kutryk of @CSA_ASC, as Earth glows below. https://t.co/DCuuNRBCJM

tweets.author: @NASA
tweets.text:
@Space_Station Teamwork! 
 
@Astro_Anil and Joshua Kutryk of @CSA_ASC have successfully unfolded the solar array, which is now extended to its full 20 ft width. https://t.co/vR48sOVF4F

tweets.author: @NASA
tweets.text:
Today’s spacewalk is:

-The 286th spacewalk supporting the @Space_Station’s assembly and maintenance
-The 9th spacewalk of 2026
-The second in one week (!) to support the installation of a solar array https://t.co/ygv8XDvEIc

tweets.author: @NASA
tweets.text: The roll-out solar array is out of its carrier and on its way to where it'll be installed. https://t.co/bUBqUsxTIG

tweets.author: @NASA
tweets.text:
Off to work we go 🎵

@astro_anil and @csa_asc's Joshua Kutryk have exited the space station and will begin their work installing the final roll-out solar array. https://t.co/D4n11ygLjg

tweets.author: @NASA
tweets.text: LIVE: Watch as @astro_anil and Joshua Kutryk of @csa_asc install the final roll-out solar array on the @space_station during a spacewalk that will last about seven hours. The solar arrays will boost power to the orbital lab. https://t.co/wAkkOdTJQR
